narrative.summaryIntro:
Guruvayur Temple in Kerala is one of the most sacred and important temples dedicated to Lord Krishna and is known as the 'Kashi of the South.' The temple's presiding deity, Guruvayurappan (Krishna), is worshipped by millions of devotees across India. According to tradition, the temple was established by Guru (Brihaspati) and Vayu (Wind God), which gives the temple its distinctive name. The temple features traditional Kerala architectural style with elaborate stone carvings and ornate decorations.

The temple is renowned for its Nalkili (sacred treasure vault) and traditional practices like Atmanathayyam (ritualistic elephant worship). It is considered one of the holiest pilgrimage destinations in South India and attracts devotees from across the world. The temple has been a center of spiritual devotion for centuries, and its connection to Krishna bhakti (devotion) makes it particularly significant. The temple also hosts several important rituals and festivals throughout the year that draw thousands of worshippers.
